sources.entry: Flock - Terminal multiplexer for running multiple Claude Code and shell sessions in one workspace. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Divagation/flock) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: flock is a native macOS app that runs many Claude Code sessions, shell panes, and editable markdown panes together in one tiled window.
summary.what_it_does: flock opens a single macOS window where you can start multiple Claude Code sessions, plain shell terminals, and markdown editing panes, which tile automatically in 1, 2, or grid layouts. Claude panes show live state indicators (thinking, working, waiting, idle) and a change log overlay listing file reads, edits, and commands. Markdown panes open or create .md files, autosave to disk, and show a conflict dialog when files change externally. Other features include a ⌘K command palette, broadcast mode that sends one input to every pane, global and per-pane find, session restore, notifications for long-running commands, a global hotkey, and an auto-updater. The README also describes optional prompt compression through a model called wren and a usage tracker for token counts and cost.
use_cases: run several Claude Code sessions side by side
monitor parallel AI coding agents in one window
mix shell terminals with Claude sessions
edit markdown notes alongside terminal work
broadcast one instruction to multiple agents
track Claude token usage and cost
how_to_run: Download the .pkg installer or .zip from the GitHub releases page
Or build from source: git clone the repository (URL not shown in README), cd flock
The app is installed to /Applications and the CLI is named flock
notable: Claude panes detect live activity from terminal output and show a ⌘⇧L change log of file reads, edits, and commands
Broadcast mode (⌘⇧B) types into every open pane at once
Native Swift app, not Electron; markdown panes are native editable text views
Optional prompt compression via wren, running locally on Apple Silicon through MLX
Seven built-in color themes including terminal ANSI palettes
caveats: macOS only; building from source requires Xcode and Swift 5.9+
Prompt compression is described as running on Apple Silicon via MLX
Plan-limit monitoring relies on the Anthropic API, as stated in the README
